title: Graph Powers — project configuration contract
description: What each repository declares in .graph-powers/config.json so the plugin can adapt to it. Every field has a safe default: a project without this file keeps working, just with the defaults. Point your config's $schema field here and your editor validates as you type. A project that only ever runs Claude Code may keep the file at .graph-powers/config.json instead; both locations are read, .graph-powers/ first.

project.description: Identity. Shows up in reports and gate messages; nothing here changes behaviour.

stack.description: Free-form stack identifier. Stack-gated skills and rules read this — 'astro' turns on the astro skill.

git.description: The git rails. Read by git_commit_gate, git_push_gate, git_branch_gate and branch_session_notice.

workBranch.description: The branch work happens on. A session that starts outside it gets a notice.

protectedBranches.description: No checkout that lands HEAD here, and no push, without an explicit opt-in in the turn.

optInPrefix.description: Prefix of the keys that release a risky action: <PREFIX>_ALLOW_COMMIT, _ALLOW_PUSH, _ALLOW_PUSH_MAIN, _ALLOW_MAIN_CHECKOUT, _ALLOW_SPAWN_OVER, _ALLOW_OFF_LEASE. Use one prefix per project: with the same key in two repositories, an approval given in one starts counting in the other.

tooling.description: The commands the gates run. Without these, a gate 'passes' because the command does not exist.

testRunner.description: null when the project has no tests — the case for static sites. Declaring null beats omitting it: it says the absence is deliberate.

commands.description: The literal command per gate. Whatever is here beats any inference.

paths.description: Where the code lives. A single app sets frontendRoot='src' and omits the rest. An empty field means the project has no such layer — plans must not invent one.

codex.description: Codex CLI specifics. Only read when generating .codex/ artefacts; ignored under Claude Code.

model.description: Model written into generated .codex/agents/*.toml. Left to the project because model names age faster than this plugin does.

reasoningEffort.description: model_reasoning_effort for generated subagents. The node that judges runs high — a cheap judge produces a false positive other nodes 'correct', and the origin of the error is lost.

skillsDir.description: Where the installer writes skills for Codex. Codex also reads ~/.agents/skills at user scope.

graphGuardrails.description: Hard ceilings on the execution graph, enforced by graph_guardrails.py. They exist to catch runaway loops, not to squeeze normal work — calibrate by measuring, not by guessing.

maxRoundsPerAgent.description: Re-spawning the same specialist many times is the signature of a loop that is not converging.

protectedFiles.description: Files no agent writes, under any circumstance. Each list extends the generic defaults; it never replaces them.

gates.description: Quality thresholds (Lighthouse, Core Web Vitals, bundle size). Consumed by the performance skill.

autonomy.description: How much the agent does without stopping to ask. This is the field that decides whether a session feels like work or like clicking Approve. Read by smart_bash_approver and the three git gates, and used by the installer to write a matching permissions allowlist.

level.description: guarded: an unrecognised command asks, and commit/push/protected-branch need an explicit opt-in key in the turn. autonomous: unrecognised commands run, cleanup runs, and the git gates pass without a key — the destructive floor below still holds. Everything under this group overrides the level individually, so 'autonomous but still ask before pushing' is one field, not a fork.

bashDefault.description: What happens to a command matching no known pattern. Defaults to ask under guarded and allow under autonomous. This single field is the source of most approval prompts.

cleanup.description: Deleting build output, caches, __pycache__, logs. Defaults to ask under guarded and allow under autonomous.

git.description: Per-action git autonomy. 'auto' means the gate passes without the opt-in key; the gate still runs and still reports what it let through.

protectedBranch.description: Checking out or pushing to a protected branch. Left at ask even under autonomous by default: it is the one git action whose blast radius is other people.

destructiveFloor.description: Keep refusing the operations git cannot undo, at any autonomy level: rm -rf on / or the home directory, mkfs, dd to a device, chmod -R 777 /, --no-preserve-root, DROP DATABASE, TRUNCATE, and force-pushing a protected branch. Deleting files inside a committed repository is not on this list — git restores those, so autonomous mode does it without asking. Set false to remove even this floor; nothing else in the harness will stop those commands.

allowPackageManagers.description: Package managers this project accepts. Empty or absent means all of them. Set it only when mixing managers actually breaks the project — a lockfile that must not fork.
